content.title: About
content.content: Nonfat mozzarella is a soft Italian cheese made from skimmed cow or buffalo milk. It has a mild, creamy flavor, elastic texture, and a characteristic white color. The low‑fat version contains minimal fat while retaining most of the protein and calcium found in traditional mozzarella.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Nonfat mozzarella is popular in diet plans and recipes where low calories are desired.
The traditional stretching (pasta) process is retained, but with reduced fat content.
The name mozzarella comes from the Italian word “mozzare,” meaning “to cut off,” referring to the way the curd is pulled.
The low‑fat version melts more easily, making it a favorite for pizza and casseroles.
While often sold in balls, it can also be sliced or grated.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Nonfat mozzarella provides about 20 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: Calcium contributes to bone and tooth health.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: Less than 2 g of fat per 100 g makes it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12 and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Phosphorus and zinc
items.content: These minerals aid metabolism and support the immune system.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to dairy or with lactose intolerance may react.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Nonfat mozzarella is often salted; those monitoring sodium should watch portions.

items.title: Product quality
items.content: Cheaper brands may contain additives and stabilizers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Mozzarella can be added to salads, used as pizza topping, baked in casseroles, sliced for sandwiches, or served as balls with vegetables. A brief warm‑up makes it softer.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated in the original packaging or an airtight container at 1‑4 °C. Once opened, it lasts 1‑2 weeks. Discard if it develops a sour smell or off‑color.
